definitions.explanation: A line made up of a series of dots or short dashes. Used in diagrams, maps, forms, and documents to indicate boundaries, cutting lines, or areas to fill in.

examples.japanese: {点線|てんせん}に{沿|そ}って{切|き}ってください。
examples.english: Please cut along the dotted line.

examples.japanese: {地図|ちず}の{点線|てんせん}は{県|けん}の{境|さかい}を{示|しめ}している。
examples.english: The dotted line on the map indicates the prefectural boundary.

examples.japanese: {点線|てんせん}の{上|うえ}に{名前|なまえ}と{住所|じゅうしょ}を{記入|きにゅう}してください。
examples.english: Please write your name and address on the dotted line.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly seen on forms, coupons, and craft instructions. The phrase {点線|てんせん}に{沿|そ}って{切|き}る (cut along the dotted line) is one of the most frequent collocations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点線|てんせん}に{沿|そ}って{切|き}る (to cut along the dotted line)
- {点線|てんせん}で{囲|かこ}む (to enclose with a dotted line)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {実線|じっせん}: solid line — a continuous, unbroken line
- {波線|なみせん}: wavy line
- {破線|はせん}: dashed line — technically distinct from dotted line, but often used interchangeably
